subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is /are true about the field around a current carrying solenoid:

(i)The field inside the solenoid is uniform.

(ii) The field outside the solenoid is same in magnitude as the field inside the solenoid.

(iii) The field around the solenoid is similar to the field around a bar magnet.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The field inside a current-carrying solenoid is uniform** because the magnetic field lines are parallel and evenly spaced inside the solenoid.
 
• The **field outside the solenoid is weak and non-uniform** compared to the field inside.
 
• The **magnetic field around a solenoid resembles that of a bar magnet**, having a north and south pole, creating a similar field pattern.
 
• The field strength inside the solenoid is determined by the current and the number of turns per unit length of the solenoid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solenoid**

 
 
• A solenoid is a coil of wire designed to create a strong magnetic field inside the coil when an electric current passes through it.
 
• Solenoids are used in various applications such as electromagnets, inductors, and actuators.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field**
 
 
• The area around a magnet where magnetic forces can be detected is called the magnetic field.
 
• Magnetic fields are visualized using magnetic field lines, which show the direction and strength of the field.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetism**
 
 
• It is the interaction between electric currents and magnetic fields.
 
• Electromagnetic phenomena include the behavior of solenoids and the generation of magnetic fields by electric currents.
 
 
 
• **Bar Magnet**
 
 
• A bar magnet is a permanent magnet in the shape of a bar with a magnetic field similar to that of a solenoid.
 
• It has two poles, north and south, and the magnetic field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole.
